headline: A 2013 law directs the Secretary of State to seek observer status for Taiwan at the International Civil Aviation Organization's 2013 Assembly and to report to Congress on the plan.
what_it_does: The law tells the Secretary of State to develop a strategy to get Taiwan observer status at the next triennial International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Assembly, held in September 2013 in Montreal. It instructs the U.S. Mission to the ICAO to formally request that status and to urge other ICAO member states to support Taiwan's observer status and participation. The Secretary must also report to Congress in unclassified form on the U.S. strategy, including for later ICAO Assemblies and related meetings.

who_it_affects.group: The Secretary of State and the State Department
who_it_affects.how: The department must develop the strategy, make the formal request through the U.S. Mission to the ICAO, and submit the unclassified report to Congress.

who_it_affects.group: The U.S. Mission to the ICAO
who_it_affects.how: The mission must officially request observer status for Taiwan and urge other member states to support it.
They are to receive the State Department's report describing the U.S. strategy.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on July 12, 2013. Its strategy was tied to the ICAO Assembly scheduled for September 2013.
